verdict: sql/038_transport_companies.sql clears the bar. All 21 acceptance criteria pass, and I verified them by execution rather than by reading: on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster with stubs for auth.users/auth.uid()/wallet_charge, the file applied FOUR times in a row under ON_ERROR_STOP with zero errors, and the §5 verify returned exactly the counts its own '-- Expect:' line predicts (tables 5, policies 7, helper 1, rpcs 5, secdef 6, guards 2, no_rig_upd 0, no_co_upd 0, no_ledger_write 0, no_cfg_pol 0, ledger_balance_cols 0, cfg_rows 1). As role 'authenticated' every write path the header claims is shut IS shut: UPDATE on companies, UPDATE on rigs, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the ledger, UPDATE on contracts and SELECT on transport_config all returned 'permission denied'; a charter insert with reliability=99 and one naming another owner were both refused by tco_ins; a rig insert carrying runs_used=9 was refused by trg_ins; a negative 'freight' ledger row was refused by the sign constraint even as superuser. No policy self-references its own table and no recursion occurs. Dispatch charged once, the same client_ref returned the same contract id without moving the balance, settle paid exactly one ledger row and recomputed reliability to 100.0 from the contract rows, a second settle returned it unchanged, an underfunded dispatch unwound the run claim in the same call, and a blacklisted shipper was refused with NO 'refused' contract row written. Every external citation I sampled is accurate against git HEAD: PP_COND_MULT at index.html:195340, playerOwnsVehicle at 195441, RARITIES at 39231, getTodayKey at 71039, OPS_ECON at 79732, the "'does not exist' does NOT mean the RPC is missing" comment at 79921, the TW-vs-uuid node postmortem at 206493-206496, and wallet_charge(bigint,text) returning (new_balance, tax_amount, ok, reason, wallet_seq) at sql/023:393-394 — which the undefined_function fallback record mirrors in the same order for the stated reason. The rejected designs are recorded with their costs (recording blocked dispatches as 'refused' rows, rejected because attempting a dispatch is free and a rival could script public refusals; auto-refunding a lost haul, rejected because it makes route risk free for the shipper and collapses the price-vs-safety choice; refusing rather than clamping an over-ceiling tariff, rejected because it punishes the one party who cannot fix the sheet), the authority is declared where two things could disagree (contract rows over the reliability cache, transport_quote as the one pricing function that dispatch calls, transport_config over the structural tariff CHECK), and the payout leg is documented as deliberately absent rather than quietly missing.
biggest_gap: The header's LIMIT-OF-THE-GUARANTEE section asserts a cap the file does not enforce. Line 147 reads 'Every one of those is capped (fleet size, runs, hops, units, price) so the blast radius is bounded' — but fleet size is capped nowhere. max_fleet_rigs (default 12) is declared in transport_config, published to the client by transport_set_sheet as 'fleet_cap', and never read by any enforcement path; trg_ins pins the counters but never counts existing rows. Running as role 'authenticated' through RLS I inserted 40 mythic rigs at runs_cap 10 into one company and all 40 landed. The client half already knows (public/src/transport/depot.js:288: '⚠ IF 038 EVER ENFORCES fleet_cap, THIS BECOMES bestDepot() TOO'), so the client-side cap is currently the only cap on a number the server publishes — the exact 'second authority' shape this file argues against elsewhere. Fix: a count check in trg_ins against least(4 * depot_level, max_fleet_rigs) via a definer helper, or strike 'fleet size' from line 147 and say plainly that fleet size is unbounded and why bays bound throughput instead.
evidence: Applied 4x with ON_ERROR_STOP, exit 0 each time; verify row returned 5|7|1|5|6|2|0|0|0|0|0|1, matching the '-- Expect:' line at sql/038_transport_companies.sql:1524-1526 exactly. FLEET CAP: `set role authenticated; insert into public.transport_rigs (...) select 'aaaaaaaa-...','1111...','mythic','Pristine',10 from generate_series(1,40);` -> 'FLEET SIZE AFTER 40 INSERTS | 40'. The claim it contradicts is sql/038:147 '-- does not hold. Every one of those is capped (fleet size, runs, hops, units,' / :148 '-- price) so the blast radius is bounded'. UNWIND STATUS: the failure branch at sql/038:1097-1103 sets `status = 'idle'` unconditionally, so after a successful haul on a rig and a second dispatch that failed at wallet_charge, `select runs_used, status from transport_rigs` returned '1 | idle' while a contract on that rig was still in_transit; the owner then deleted the rig under trg_del (sql/038:588-589, `using (owner_id = auth.uid() and status <> 'hauling')`), leaving 'ORPHANED IN-TRANSIT CONTRACT | 8345f661-... | (null rig_id) | in_transit' — which the trg_del comment at :585-587 says must not be possible ('retiring one mid-haul is not, because the contract would keep an arrival time nobody is driving towards'). RLS denials as authenticated: 'ERROR: permission denied for table transport_config / transport_companies / transport_rigs / transport_ledger / transport_contracts', and 'ERROR: new row violates row-level security policy for table "transport_companies"' for both a reliability=99 insert and an insert naming another owner. Ledger sign: 'ERROR: new row for relation "transport_ledger" violates check constraint "transport_ledger_sign_ck"' on amount=-5000 kind='freight' as superuser. Money path: DISPATCH1 price 2000, balance 998000; DISPATCH1-RETRY returned retried:true with the same contract_id and the balance unchanged; SETTLE amount 2000 status delivered; SETTLE-RETRY retried:true; ledger count 1 sum 2000; reliability 100.0. set_sheet clamped {"base":9999999,"escort_pct":500,"bogus":42} to {"base":500,"escort_pct":100,"illicit_pct":0}, dropping the unknown key. greps: 5 'enable row level security', 7 create policy, 0 hits for wallet_credit / discord / webhook / pg_net, `using (true)` appears once (sql/038:526, transport_companies, commented as the public rate board), and no policy body names its own table. Header provenance caveat: the only PostgreSQL init attempt surviving in the scratchpad is /tmp/.../scratchpad/pg/init.log at 02:57, which FAILED with 'initdb: error: could not access directory ... Permission denied' three minutes before the file was written at 03:00, and no cluster exists anywhere on this box outside the untouched Mar-31 system one — so I could not corroborate that the author personally ran the four applications the '📋 WHAT WAS ACTUALLY MEASURED' block describes. Every specific claim in that block that I could test independently was true, including the oddly specific ones, so I am recording the ambiguity rather than calling it fabricated.
